newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: European feeds dampened by holidays, ice blockages.
newsitem.headline: European feeds dampened by holidays, ice blockages.

text.p: European meals and feeds failed to pick up substantial buying interest on Friday despite a slightly softer Chicago opening as consumers remained either absent from the market or pre-occupied with ice-blocked canals.
"I think we'll have to wait until the middle of next week before things get back to normal," one trader said, adding that this depended on the ice situation not getting any worse.

The Rhine remained navigable from Rotterdam to Basle but the freeze had hit its tributaries, hampering barge movements through Benelux and Germany. Conditions were severest in Germany where most Rhine tributuries were closed or partially blocked.
"The Mosel is closed and there are many difficulties on the Main," said one German barge operator.
"It's getting steadily worse and worse," another barge operator said.
Meals and feed trades were restricted largely to rapemeal, with some done on a free-on-truck basis because of the ice problems. There was no trade in soymeal or sunmeal reported.

Traders described this afternoon's U.S. crop production estimates by the commodity advisory firm Sparks as neutral. It estimated the corn crop at 9.295 billion bushels and the soybean crop at 2.403 billion. -- Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
